newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to give $670,000 in aid to Albania.
newsitem.headline: Japan to give $670,000 in aid to Albania.

text.p: Japan will give $670,000 in aid to Albania through the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), the Foreign Ministry said on Tuesday.
Japan's move follows similar steps by the United States, the European Union and other European countries to aid the Balkan state as it copes with near-anarchy conditions.
According to the ICRC, 70,000 families, or 10 percent of Albania's population of 3.4 million, need humanitarian aid.
Widespread civil strife erupted in Albania after the collapse in February of fraudulent savings schemes in which many people had invested their life savings.
A U.N.-approved multinational security mission, to eventually total 6,000 troops from eight countries, will deploy in force on Tuesday to protect agencies distributing aid.
The Geneva-based ICRC had distributed 40 tonnes of food and 15 tonnes of medicine in Albania since March 27, an ICRC spokeswoman said on Monday.
